No data-as-code in the v142 sample. I checked all 45 accepted sites against original_ROMs/kn5000_subprogram_v142.rom (file offset = address - 0x0EF00). Every src_addr holds the stated branch opcode (jr 6x, jrl 7x, calr 1e, call 1d, jp 1b), and every recomputed target equals the tool's target. Every source reads as compiler-generated C code: consistent (xsp+N) frame use, the muls wa,287 part-record indexing, arguments set up before calls, for-loop pre-checks and back-edges, and switch range checks. Sources come from the Audio_Cmd_*, VoiceParam_*, DSP_* and TaskSched sections of v142/subcpu/kn5000_subprogram_v142.s. The sites inside the DSP bytecode handlers (DSP_Bytecode_Programs, DSP_Bytecode_Op04/Op05, around lines 56065-56720) were converted from `.byte` runs, but they are coherent code and their call targets are DSP_DispatchCommand/DSP_DispatchData. The one data-framed target (site 24, FIFO_Engine1K_Get_Marked at 0x020BBB, around line 2320) decodes cleanly under unidasm as FIFO engine code: the neighbouring `.byte` runs at 0x020A9D..0x020C?? are undisassembled code, not data.

Only failure pattern found is in label NAMING, not source classification:
1. The prefix is inherited from the nearest preceding label even when the target is a routine-wide exit. VoiceParam_Set_Tone_Option_Case0_Join (0x02E918, sites 19/31/36) is the common `inc 4,xsp; ret` epilogue of VoiceParam_Set_Tone_Option, reached from the pre-switch range checks and all 7 cases. Naming it Case0_* tells the reader the out-of-range default belongs to case 0.
2. Frame-drop epilogues (`inc N,xsp; ret`, `lda xsp,(xsp+N); ret`, `ld hl,iz; popw iz; inc 6,xsp; ret`) do not match the Epilogue rule, which requires pops then ret, so they become Join. Examples: 0x02E918 and DSP_SetCoeff_MasterConfig_Join at 0x031A51. Suggested guard: treat `inc N,xsp`/`lda xsp,(xsp+N)` as a pop-equivalent. When every source of a new label lies between the enclosing routine entry and the target, derive the name from the routine entry label rather than the nearest intermediate case label.
3. Minor: DSP_Bytecode_Programs_Join2 (0x03C554, site 15) inherits the legacy DSP_Bytecode_Programs name, which the source comment says covers CODE (handler 0). It is not wrong, but the "Programs" prefix suggests data. That target is really a for-loop condition check (LoopCond), not a plain join.

Dead-but-real code shows up as sources (DSP_SetCoeff_WithDispatch, CheckStatusBits_80, both documented as unreferenced). Their branches are internally consistent, so labelling them is harmless.

patterns:
No data decoded as code turned up in this sample. All 45 sources are real code and all 45 targets are plausible. I checked the ones that looked odd (sites 0, 8, 12, 19, 22, 30, 35, 42, 44 and several of the absolute-jp targets) against the ROM bytes in original_ROMs/hd-ae5000_v2_06i.ic4 with unidasm. Every displacement lands on an instruction boundary, and callers and targets agree on how stack arguments are passed and cleaned up. Every structural role is right: each Loop is backward, each Join is unconditional, each Sub is reached only by calls.

The label_misleading problems all come from existing names or inherited prefixes, not from the tool's role logic.

(1) Four existing hand-written labels are wrong. The tool reuses them correctly, so fix the labels rather than blocking the sites:
- HDAE5000_Divide_Signed at 0x29B8C5 (hdae5000/hdae5000_utilities.s) is the unsigned divide core; the signed wrapper is at 0x29B870.
- HDAE5000_Display_Sub_294414 (hdae5000/hdae5000_ui_display.s:14373, commented 'Large display management routine (3061 bytes)') is one byte of 0x0E, a compiled-out debug-trace stub. Every caller passes XWA = a '---[ Name ]---' banner string from around 0x2f8f5e-0x2f92xx.
- HDAE5000_StrCopy at 0x29AF0B is strcat.
- Several local .L labels are used as cross-file subroutine targets: .Lccb_sign_handler (called from hdae5000_hd_driver.s), .Lppc_send_region_to_pc, .Lppc_utility and .Lpsb_finish. This assembles, because hd-ae5000_v2_06i.s .includes every part into one unit. But .L symbols never reach the ELF symbol table, so they are invisible to the symbols/ files and to llvm-objdump.

(2) New names built from the enclosing region label are semantically wrong even when the role is right. Old coarse labels such as 'LDS 3061 bytes', 'LDIV 1819 bytes' and 'LTCI 2171 bytes' each span many functions. That produces names like:
- HDAE5000_Display_Sub_294414_SubN (sites 42 and 44). These are children of a ret stub, and they carry an address, against the no-address-names policy.
- HDAE5000_Display_String_Render_* and HDAE5000_RAM_Test_* on HD self-test and sector I/O code around 0x2974xx-0x2999xx (IDE status polling at 0x13001E, error codes stored to 0x200222).
- HDAE5000_Multiply_SubN on double-copy and float-conversion helpers (0x29B7DC is a va_arg 8-byte copy).
- Very large suffixes such as Loop44 and Sub23 are a sign that the parent region is not one function.

Suggested guard: when the parent label's region is larger than a few hundred bytes, or the parent is a bare ret, or the parent name contains a hex address, fall back to a neutral name (e.g. HDAE5000_Sub_<role>) instead of inheriting the prefix.

(3) The one recurring 'suspicious-looking' pattern is actual code: the nop-interleaved PPORT code in hdae5000/hdae5000_ui_display.s, roughly 0x2951xx-0x297xxx. That is the hand-annotated parallel-port driver with timing nops, and the 8-byte `call X; ld wa,hl; ret; nop` stubs at .Lpps_handler_N. A heuristic of 'nop runs mean data' would wrongly reject these.

Files and ranges to watch in other hdae5000 samples: hdae5000/hdae5000_data_tables.s (not represented here), and anything inside the region labels above.

No data-as-code in the prom_c sample: all 45 sites are REAL_CODE with a sound target. I checked every site against wsa1/original_ROMs/wsa1_prom_c.ic28 (base 0xF80000). Each source address holds 1D <lo> <mid> <hi> (call imm24) encoding exactly the claimed target. Each target is an existing routine entry: a link32 prologue (EE 0C ..) or, for MemCopyWords, Shift8_LogicalRight and Flash_ProgramSectorFromBuffer, a leaf that reads (xsp+N). Many targets have tens to hundreds of callers (Double_Multiply 230, Float32_ToDouble 169, Double_ToFloat32 164). The sample has a blind spot. For prom_c the tool's own census counts 2,479 numeric branch operands, and my regex finds 2,467 call, 25 jrl and 12 jp. So random sampling almost never picks a relative branch, and this sample says nothing about the risky jr/jrl/calr path or the new-label naming path.

I read the unsampled numeric jrl sites by hand, and they are also real code:
- wsa1/prom_c/tone_db/tone_db_module.s, lines 14747-14785: a compiled switch chain (`cp bc,N / jrl z, -0xNNN`, 20 arms).
- The same file, lines 11705, 13392, 13902 and 14739: backward `jrl -0xEE` / `-0xE2` just after `.long` computed-goto tables. Each is at a real label boundary, so these are loop/join back-edges, not bytes of the tables.

The 12 `jp 0xF9xxxx` lines in wsa1/prom_c/boot/reset_and_vectors.s target the shared kernel region, which should be excluded as shared-file.

Guard suggestions:
- Stratify review samples by mnemonic (call vs jr/jrl/calr/jp) and by new-vs-reused label. For prom_c, review all 25 jrl sites directly, since that is cheap.
- The main thing to watch in the jrl sites is the placement right after `.long` jump tables. Check that a label planted there is never inside a `.long` run: the table-end boundary must be the target, not a byte inside the table.

Coverage gap, not a failure: roughly 1,490 prom_c branches use the address-difference form `calr (0xTGT - 0xNEXT)` or `jr/jrl (0xTGT - 0xNEXT)`. The main concentrations are p7_module.s (492), tone_db_module.s (290), voice_parameters.s (210) and midi_controllers.s (179). No data-as-code found in the 45 prom_b sites. All 45 source and target addresses land on instruction boundaries in MAME's linear listing wsa1/original_ROMs/wsa1_prom_b.ic13.unidasm, and every context reads as coherent code: consistent register use, balanced push/pop, compiler-style link/pushw/inc-XSP sequences, switch chains with regular displacement steps. Targets in the jp-trampoline tables (T_F40Cxx, T_F427xx, T_F431xx in wsa1/prom_b/wsa1_prom_b.s around lines 81800-84200) are correct 4-byte slot boundaries. For prom_b the accepted set looks clean. I found no file or label family that is consistently data-as-code.

Three things for tightening the guard or the naming:

(1) Dead-but-real jump runs. Unreachable consecutive jrl/jr instructions all resolve to one target: F75E4A-F75E53 (4 x jrl to F75AD2, in the body of sub_F75685) and the duplicate `jrl 128` at F64098. A guard that required 'source reached by the walk' would reject these, but they are code artefacts rather than data. The telltale is several consecutive branches converging on one target at a regular stride, which is a good positive code signal. The reverse is the data-as-code signature to guard against: branches in a run that scatter to unrelated or odd targets.

(2) Over-wide routine extents. The 'Extent' walk for sub_F001C9 (wsa1_prom_b.s about line 575; it claims F001C9-F0027F) spans about 5 separate ret-delimited subroutines (entries at F0020B, F0023C, F00240, F00244). As a result, calr targets there get names like sub_F001C9_Sub4 instead of standalone sub_F00244. The prefix is not a hazard, but it attributes a separate routine to the wrong parent. The same is likely in other lane-promB6 'converted CODE' spans near F00000-F00300. Suggested rule: when every source is a call and the target directly follows a `ret`, name it sub_<target>.

(3) Side finding, not a branch issue. The LLVM backend encodes `di` as 06 00, which MAME decodes as `ei 0x00`: IFF=0, all interrupts enabled. The real DI is 06 07, and MAME prints that as `ei 0x07`. So all 27 `di` lines in wsa1/prom_b/wsa1_prom_b.s (e.g. F0008D and F00091, which close an `ei 6` critical section) read as the opposite of what the CPU does. This also applies to any other tree that uses `di` with this backend.

SAMPLE RESULT (prom_a, 45 sites): every source is real code (45/45). 44/45 targets are clean instruction boundaries. Site 2 lands in undisassembled code framed as .byte. No data-as-code source was in the sample. The problems found are in NAMING, plus two accepted data-as-code sources that I found outside the sample.

1. PARENT NAMING INHERITS DATA LABELS (symbolize_numeric_branches.py, lines 442-451). Parent = the nearest preceding label that does not start with .L. When that label names a table, the arm code after the table gets a table name. In prom_a.json labels_new, 11 of the 49 new labels are JumpTable_*: F9A414, F9ABEB, FAC38A, FB20C3, FB20CD, FB63A9, FC8E5E, FC8E6E (site 28), FD70F0, FD712A, FD7152. Others with the same problem: RecordTable_F8C727_Skip (F8C746), MidiIn_ControlRecordHandlers_Join/_Skip (FABFDC/FABFDD), Evt2030_ClassHandlers_Return (FAE800), Evt2030_Class20to3F_Return (FADCCA), Fdc_OperationJumpTable_Entry (FE6E80) and Data_FF17E2_Entry (FF2232). Fix: skip any candidate parent whose first emitting line is data (.byte/.short/.long/.fill). Otherwise fall back to sub_/L plus the target's own address. The positional '<prev>_Sub' / '_SubN' names for standalone routines after a ret (sub_F97533_Sub, sub_F97418_Sub3) also mislead mildly. A standalone routine should get sub_<own addr>.

2. Data_FF17E2 IS MIS-BOUNDED (wsa1/prom_a/wsa1_prom_a.s:173586-173768). Its tail 0xFF21F6-0xFF2269 is four real subroutines (FF21F6, FF2204, FF2232, FF224D) with dozens of callers. The header line 'Nothing else in either image names any address inside it' is false. The tool labels FF2232 only because it happens to start a 16-byte .byte row. FF21F6 and FF2204 fall mid-row, so they are refused as mid-line-data. A boundary-data target with call sources should be reported as SPLIT+DISASSEMBLE rather than named Data_X_Entry.

3. DATA-AS-CODE THAT THE GUARDS ACCEPTED (outside the sample):
(a) wsa1_prom_a.s:172608: `jrl z, 0x40f1` at FF0BF0, the first 'instruction' after DisplayList_FF0BE1's last .byte row, with no label in between. The byte 0x76 at FF0BF0 is data: the op-02 display-list records point at it (pointer bytes at FF0BD9/FF0BE8). The real routine starts at FF0BF1 with f1 40 25 00 00 = ld (0x2540),0, the same opening as sub_FF0C12. The bogus jrl lands at FF4CE4, in the middle of a push sequence in LcdKeyRow4_DiskL0adFile, and the tool plans a new label there, LcdKeyRow4_DiskL0adFile_Skip. None of R1/R2/R3 fires: the block has 10 instructions, its other branches hit boundaries, and it holds only one nop. About 1% of the sites the tool accepted in v10 are fake branches. The byte gate cannot catch them. I checked every accepted site against the ROM's own disassembly: 86 of 8,028 (1.07%) sit at an address where the ROM has no instruction start, or where the byte there is not that branch opcode. 13 of those 86 also point at a mid-instruction address; the other 73 hit a real instruction start by chance, so their labels look fine but come from a branch that does not exist. In this sample, site 26 is the one fake.

Method: I imported the current script's `analyse()` read-only and checked each accepted site against `original_ROMs/kn5000_v10_program.rom.unidasm`. A branch opcode means 0x60-6F for jr, 0x70-7F for jrl, 0x1E calr, 0x1D call, 0x1B jp.
- Script: `scratchpad/audit_v10.py`; results: `scratchpad/v10_audit.json`.
- The scratchpad is shared with sibling agents and is volatile. A sibling already overwrote my `sites.txt`, so commit the check if you adopt it.

**1. Fake branches from converter desync (the main failure).** The ASL-to-LLVM conversion sometimes writes an instruction's first byte as a lone `.byte` and decodes the remaining operand bytes as separate instructions. Typical lone bytes are 0xf1/0xc1/0xd1/0xe1 (16-bit address forms) and 0x8f/0x9f/0xbf (stack-offset forms). When an operand byte falls in 0x60-7F or is 0x1E, a phantom `jr`/`jrl`/`calr` appears. Examples:
- `bit 2,(0xc07f)` (f1 7f c0 ca) becomes `.byte 0xf1 / jrl nc,-13632`.
- `cp (0x287a),0` becomes `.byte 0xc1 / jrl gt,16168 / nop`.
- `add hl,(xsp+2); inc 6,xsp; ret` becomes `.byte 0x9f / push sr / or (xhl),l / jr z,14` (site 26).

The same desync also hides real branches, for example inside `.ascii "h&Ph"`, `scc8 nz,b` and `decm8 6,(xiz)/zcf`.

The existing R3 check misses these because the garbage looks plausible: a single `nop`, `push sr`, `or (xhl),l`, `ld (N:8),M:io`, `jr ov`, `xor (xsp),xhl`.

**Recommended guard:** accept a site only if its address is an instruction start in an independent ROM disassembly and the byte there is the right branch opcode. For v10 that drops exactly the 86 fakes.
- Also require the target to be an instruction start.
- For images without a ready listing, run unidasm from the nearest label.
- A source-only rule ("a `.byte` line within the previous 3 code lines") would catch 80 of the 86 but also reject 659 good sites.
- Extra warning signs worth adding to R3: `jr/jrl` with ov/nov/pe/po/mi/pl conditions, and `:io` direct-page operands or `(xsp),xhl` forms right after a lone `.byte`.

**2. The 'Entry' role is usually wrong.** Most of v10's 393 data-framed targets are real code that the converter split into `.byte` fragments. Example: `ldw (0x26de),(0x2632)` became `.byte 0xd1 / ldw de,6438 / .byte 0xde`. Mid-routine skip and join points therefore get names like `SeqPart_ByteBlockB0DE_Entry` (site 0) and `UIStateEvt_ChannelConfig_Data_Entry6` (site 37). Work the role out from the sources the same way as for code targets, and keep the data framing out of the name.

**3. The 'Loop' role is wrong for tail-jumps and switch joins.** Any backward source currently makes a Loop. Two misfires in the sample:
- Site 32: F971E1 is a subroutine entry reached by backward `jrl T` tail calls plus 12 `calr`.
- Site 44: F349B2 is a switch-case shared tail reached by backward `jr T`.

The tool proposes 397 new Loop labels in v10. 7 of them are also call/calr targets, so they are certainly subroutine entries. 75 have only unconditional backward sources, which is an upper bound on how many are misnamed. Suggested fix: prefer Sub when any source is a call/calr and the target follows a `ret` or an unconditional jump. Use Loop only when a backward source is conditional, or when there is no unconditional exit between the target and that source.

**4. Names inherited from wrong existing labels.** Names such as `_ByteBlock*`, `_Data`, `_DataBlock*`, `_Bytecode*`, `_InlineData`, `_JumpTable`, `_DisplayStrings`, `_TableDataEntry` and `Data_*` sit on genuine code. The tool copies them into new names (sites 0, 3, 4, 6, 7, 13, 14, 16, 18, 19, 27, 30, 37, 38, 39). This is not a role error, but it reinforces the old mistakes.

**5. Reusing an existing label can mislead.** `MidiStream_ExtendedDispatch` (site 35) sits on a one-byte `ret` stub at FCCB1C. The real routine starts one byte later at FCCB1D, labelled `MidiStream_ExtendedDispatch_0x1`.

**Two further notes:**
- Sites 20, 21, 24, 29, 33 and 36 show that `.byte`-prefix renderings often line up again before the sampled branch. Only a check against the ROM separates those from site 26.
- The proposed names in the sample come from an older revision of the tool. The current script names 20 of the 45 targets differently; for example site 0 is now `SeqPart_DualCopySetup_Entry3`, site 32 is `FDC_Wait_Status_Timeout_Loop` and site 26 is `Flash_WriteBackSlotTable_Skip`. The problems in items 1-3 are still present in the current names.

I checked each of the 45 sampled branches and targets against original_ROMs/kn5000_v7_program.rom, decoding at the ROM addresses myself.

- The 7 misleading-name verdicts (sites 9, 12, 19, 20, 21, 34, 40) come from naming, not from data-as-code.

Outside the sample, I rebuilt the accepted set from scratchpad/symbr/v7.json: all numeric branches minus the R1/R2/R3/external/mid-line refusals. That found real data-as-code that the guard accepted.

(1) CONFIRMED data-as-code accepted, in v7/maincpu/extensions/extension_data.s: 5 sites, all of them bad.
- Lines 129 and 130: the "min  " chord string decoded as `jr pl,0x69` and `jr nz,32`.
- Lines 163, 166 and 169: the pointer table `xx 02 ed 00` (0x00ED02xx entries) decoded as `jr nov,2`, `jr 2`, `jr le,2` between `.byte 0xed / nop`.

  - refuse any site within a few lines of `aligned_string`/`.ascii`;
  - refuse a jr cc whose opcode byte and displacement byte are both printable ASCII (0x60-0x6F plus 0x20-0x7E) when the surrounding ROM bytes are more than 80% printable and NUL-terminated;
  - refuse when the ±16 bytes of ROM form at least 4 consecutive little-endian 32-bit values in 0xE00000-0xFFFFFF (a pointer table).
- Refusing the whole of extension_data.s would cost nothing: 491 of its 496 sites are already refused.

(2) Possible edge case to check: R3 appears not to see the first numeric branch of a file.
